question: A 47-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of a lump on her neck and a 1-week history of hoarseness. Examination shows a 3-cm, firm, non-tender nodule on the anterior neck. Further evaluation confirms a thyroid malignancy, and she undergoes thyroidectomy. Histopathologic examination of the surgical specimen shows lymphatic invasion. Genetic analysis shows an activating mutation in the RET/PTC genes. Microscopic examination of the surgical specimen is most likely to also show which of the following?

options.opa: Pleomorphic giant cells with numerous atypical mitotic figures
options.opb: Sheets of polygonal cells surrounding amyloid deposition
options.opc: Calcified spherules and large oval cells with empty-appearing nuclei
options.opd: Cuboidal cells arranged spherically around colloid lakes

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Thyroid malignancy" -> "Thyroidectomy performed" -> "Histopathologic examination shows lymphatic invasion" -> "Activating mutation in RET/PTC genes" -> "Microscopic examination likely to show sheets of polygonal cells surrounding amyloid deposition" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Thyroid malignancy" -> "Thyroidectomy performed" -> "Histopathologic examination shows lymphatic invasion" -> "Activating mutation in RET/PTC genes" -> "Microscopic examination likely to show pleomorphic giant cells with numerous atypical mitotic figures" -> 70%
analysis: The presence of lymphatic invasion and an activating mutation in the RET/PTC genes in a thyroid malignancy suggests a papillary thyroid carcinoma. The characteristic histologic feature of papillary thyroid carcinoma is the presence of cuboidal cells arranged spherically around colloid lakes, known as papillae.
